stroganina.name: Stroganina
stroganina.summary: A dish of raw, thin-sliced frozen fish eaten by northern Russians and Indigenous Siberian peoples, popular in several Siberian cuisines.

yakutian-knife.name: Yakutian knife
yakutian-knife.summary: A traditional asymmetrical-bladed knife of the Yakuts of Siberia, used for working wood, hides and meat or fish.

winnipeg-art-gallery.name: Winnipeg Art Gallery
winnipeg-art-gallery.summary: Art museum in Winnipeg, Canada, whose permanent collection of over 24,000 works includes the world's largest collection of Inuit art.

museum-of-inuit-art.name: Museum of Inuit Art
museum-of-inuit-art.summary: Museum in Toronto devoted exclusively to Inuit art and culture, open from 2007 until it closed in 2016.

kinngait.name: Kinngait
kinngait.summary: An Inuit hamlet on Dorset Island near Baffin Island in Nunavut, Canada, known as Cape Dorset until 2020.

ovilu-tunnillie.name: Ovilu Tunnillie
ovilu-tunnillie.summary: An Inuk sculptor (1949–2014) from Baffin Island known for autobiographical carvings addressing traditional and changing Inuit life, shaped by the trauma of forced tuberculosis removal as a child.

canadian-museum-of-history.name: Canadian Museum of Civilization
canadian-museum-of-history.summary: A national museum in Gatineau, Quebec, on Canadian history and anthropology, known as the Canadian Museum of Civilization from 1990 to 2013 before being renamed.

hudson-s-bay-company.name: Hudson's Bay Company
hudson-s-bay-company.summary: A Canadian company founded in 1670 that controlled the North American fur trade and acted as the de facto government of British North America until 1869, later becoming a department store chain before liquidating in 2025.

west-baffin-eskimo-cooperative.name: West Baffin Eskimo Cooperative
west-baffin-eskimo-cooperative.summary: An Inuit co-operative founded in 1959 in Kinngait, Nunavut, that has bought, produced and sold over 100,000 Inuit artworks since its founding.

floyd-kuptana.name: Floyd Kuptana
floyd-kuptana.summary: Inuvialuk artist in Canada (1964–2021) known mainly for stone carvings, as well as paintings and collage, part of the modern Inuit art movement that grew from the late 1940s on.

cape-parry.name: Cape Parry
cape-parry.summary: A headland in Canada's Northwest Territories named after Arctic explorer William Edward Parry, once served by a now-abandoned airport near a Cold War radar station.

distant-early-warning-line.name: Distant Early Warning Line
distant-early-warning-line.summary: Cold War-era chain of radar stations across Arctic Canada, Alaska, Greenland and Iceland, built to give early warning of a Soviet bomber attack.

abraham-anghik-ruben.name: Abraham Anghik Ruben
abraham-anghik-ruben.summary: Inuvialuk Canadian sculptor of Yup'ik descent, born in 1951 near Paulatuk in Canada's Northwest Territories, inducted into the Order of Canada in 2016.

david-ruben-piqtoukun.name: David Ruben Piqtoukun
david-ruben-piqtoukun.summary: Inuvialuk (Inuk) artist from Paulatuk, Northwest Territories (1950–2026).

library-and-archives-canada.name: Library and Archives Canada
library-and-archives-canada.summary: Canada's federal institution for preserving and providing access to the country's documentary heritage, formed in 2004 by merging its national archives and national library.

glenbow-museum.name: Glenbow Museum
glenbow-museum.summary: An art and history museum in Calgary, Canada, founded in 1955, focused on Western Canadian history and Indigenous perspectives.

arkhangelsk.name: Arkhangelsk
arkhangelsk.summary: A Russian city on the White Sea that was the country's chief seaport until 1703, later a key destination for Arctic supply convoys during World War II.

murmansk.name: Murmansk
murmansk.summary: Port city in far northwest Russia on Kola Bay, the world's largest city north of the Arctic Circle, kept ice-free by a warm Atlantic current.

petsamo-kirkenes-offensive.name: Petsamo–Kirkenes offensive
petsamo-kirkenes-offensive.summary: A 1944 World War II offensive in which the Red Army defeated German forces in the Arctic, drove them into Norway, and seized the Petsamo nickel mines.

arctic-star.name: Arctic Star
arctic-star.summary: A British military campaign medal created in 2012 for veterans who served on the Arctic Convoys north of the Arctic Circle during the Second World War.

winston-churchill.name: Winston Churchill
winston-churchill.summary: British statesman and Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1940 to 1945 and 1951 to 1955, who led Britain through the Second World War.

battle-of-the-barents-sea.name: Battle of the Barents Sea
battle-of-the-barents-sea.summary: A World War II naval battle on 31 December 1942 in which German warships failed to destroy a British-escorted Arctic convoy, a failure so infuriating to Hitler it shifted German strategy toward submarines.

convoy-jw-51b.name: Convoy JW 51B
convoy-jw-51b.summary: A December 1942 Arctic convoy carrying Allied supplies to the Soviet Union that fended off a German naval attack in what became the Battle of the Barents Sea.

adolf-hitler.name: Adolf Hitler
adolf-hitler.summary: Austrian-born German dictator who led Nazi Germany from 1933 until his suicide in 1945, launching the Second World War and directing the Holocaust.

german-battleship-tirpitz.name: Tirpitz
german-battleship-tirpitz.summary: A German Bismarck-class battleship commissioned in 1941, named after Admiral Alfred von Tirpitz, that threatened Allied convoys from Norway until it was sunk in 1944.

convoy-pq-12.name: Convoy PQ 12
convoy-pq-12.summary: A March 1942 Arctic convoy to Murmansk that the German battleship Tirpitz failed to intercept, though it lost two ships to storms and ice along the way.

spitsbergen.name: Spitsbergen
spitsbergen.summary: The largest island of Norway's Svalbard archipelago in the Arctic, used as a whaling base in the 17th and 18th centuries and later for coal mining.

narsarsuaq-air-base.name: Bluie West One
narsarsuaq-air-base.summary: A U.S. Army base built in southern Greenland from 1941, a key link in the North Atlantic air-ferry route in World War II, through which some 10,000 aircraft passed to Europe and North Africa.

greenland-patrol.name: Greenland Patrol
greenland-patrol.summary: A World War II U.S. Coast Guard operation supporting U.S. Army airfield building in Greenland, guarding against German activity, escorting Allied shipping, and running rescue and weather services from 1941 to 1945.

naval-detachment-k.name: Naval Detachment K
naval-detachment-k.summary: A Finnish naval flotilla that operated on Lake Ladoga during World War II.

ib-knud-poulsen.name: Ib Poulsen
ib-knud-poulsen.summary: A Danish-born captain of Greenland's Sirius Patrol (1909–1994), the only person in history to directly command the Patrol and the sole historic commander of the 'Army of Greenland,' and a Legion of Merit recipient.

eske-brun.name: Eske Brun
eske-brun.summary: Danish civil servant and governor of Greenland (1904–1987), connected to the territory from 1932 to 1964.

h-kon-nilsen.name: Håkon Nilsen
h-kon-nilsen.summary: Norwegian naval officer (1913–1976), nicknamed 'Torpedo Nilsen', a highly decorated World War II torpedo commander.

hnoms-stord.name: HNoMS Stord
hnoms-stord.summary: A Royal Norwegian Navy S-class destroyer acquired from the Royal Navy in 1943, one of two vessels named after the island of Stord; it was broken up in 1959.

barry-lopez.name: Barry Lopez
barry-lopez.summary: American essayist and nature writer (1945–2020) who wrote about landscapes including the Arctic; his book Arctic Dreams won the 1986 National Book Award for Nonfiction.

arctic-dreams.name: Arctic Dreams
arctic-dreams.summary: A 1986 nonfiction book by Barry Lopez about the Arctic landscape, its wildlife and the relationship between people and nature, winner of the National Book Award for Nonfiction.

henning-jakob-henrik-lund.name: Henrik Lund
henning-jakob-henrik-lund.summary: Greenlandic lyricist, painter, and Lutheran pastor (1875 to 1948) who wrote the lyrics to Greenland's national anthem, "Nunarput, utoqqarsuanngoravit."

nunarput-utoqqarsuanngoravit.name: Nunarput utoqqarsuanngoravit
nunarput-utoqqarsuanngoravit.summary: Greenland's national anthem, written in 1912 by Henning Jakob Henrik Lund and set to music by Jonathan Petersen in 1937, officially adopted in 1916.

jonathan-petersen.name: Jonathan Petersen
jonathan-petersen.summary: Greenlandic songwriter (1881–1961) who composed the music for Greenland's national anthem, adopted in 1916, and wrote the words and music of its secondary anthem.

the-voyage-of-the-arctic-tern.name: The Voyage of the Arctic Tern
the-voyage-of-the-arctic-tern.summary: Hugh Montgomery's first book, a children's verse novel illustrated by Nick Poullis about an ancient ship's captain cursed with eternal life who seeks redemption; published in 2002 after winning self-publishing awards.
the-voyage-of-the-arctic-tern.source_title: The Voyage of the Arctic Tern

michiko-kakutani.name: Michiko Kakutani
michiko-kakutani.summary: American writer and retired literary critic (born 1955) who reviewed books for The New York Times from 1983 to 2017, winning the 1998 Pulitzer Prize for Criticism.

robert-macfarlane-writer.name: Robert Macfarlane
robert-macfarlane-writer.summary: British non-fiction writer and Cambridge fellow known for books on landscape and nature such as The Old Ways and Underland, and twice named an outside contender for the Nobel Prize in Literature.

nanortalik.name: Nanortalik
nanortalik.summary: A town in southern Greenland whose name means 'Place of Polar Bears,' now the southernmost Greenlandic town with over 1,000 residents.

hood-river-nunavut.name: Hood River
hood-river-nunavut.summary: A 400 km river in Nunavut, Canada, draining into the Arctic Ocean, named after Lieutenant Robert Hood, who was murdered on Franklin's first overland expedition.

baffin-bay.name: Baffin Bay
baffin-bay.summary: A marginal sea of the Arctic Ocean between Baffin Island and Greenland, connected to the Atlantic Ocean via the Davis Strait and Labrador Sea.

beaufort-sea.name: Beaufort Sea
beaufort-sea.summary: A sea of the Arctic Ocean north of Alaska and Canada, named after hydrographer Francis Beaufort and historically frozen for most of the year.

ammassalik-island.name: Ammassalik Island
ammassalik-island.summary: An island in southeastern Greenland's Sermersooq municipality, about 772 square kilometers in area, also known by its Danish name Kong Oscars Ø.

augo-lynge.name: Augo Lynge
augo-lynge.summary: Greenlandic politician, educator, poet and novelist (1899–1959) who became the first Greenlandic representative in the Danish parliament and died in the sinking of the MS Hans Hedtoft.

knud-rasmussen.name: Knud Rasmussen
knud-rasmussen.summary: A Greenlandic-Danish polar explorer and anthropologist (1879–1933), called the 'father of Eskimology', and the first European to cross the Northwest Passage by dog sled.

hinrich-johannes-rink.name: Hinrich Johannes Rink
hinrich-johannes-rink.summary: A Danish geologist and glaciology pioneer (1819–1893) who spent years in Greenland, became its scholar and administrator, introduced early home rule, and made the first systematic collection of Greenlandic oral tradition.

robert-peary.name: Robert Peary
robert-peary.summary: American Arctic explorer and naval officer credited with reaching the North Pole in 1909, though this is now doubted; proved Greenland an island and studied Inuit survival skills.

greenland-ice-sheet.name: Greenland ice sheet
greenland-ice-sheet.summary: Greenland has had major glaciers and ice caps for at least 18 million years, with a single ice sheet covering most of the island for about 2.6 million years; its oldest ice is roughly 1 million years old.

international-arctic-science-committee.name: International Arctic Science Committee
international-arctic-science-committee.summary: A non-governmental international scientific organization founded in 1990 by the eight Arctic countries, now including 25 countries coordinating Arctic research.

resolute-nunavut.name: Resolute Bay
resolute-nunavut.summary: An Inuit hamlet on Cornwallis Island in Nunavut, Canada, at the northern end of Resolute Bay and the Northwest Passage.

jakobshavn-glacier.name: Jakobshavn Glacier
jakobshavn-glacier.summary: Large outlet glacier in West Greenland that drains 6.5% of the ice sheet and produces about 10% of Greenland's icebergs, studied for over 250 years.

yellow-river-station.name: Yellow River Station
yellow-river-station.summary: A Chinese Arctic research station in Ny-Alesund, Svalbard (Norway), operating year-round with room for 18 staff and about 50 researchers a year.

svalbard.name: Svalbard
svalbard.summary: A Norwegian Arctic archipelago between mainland Norway and the North Pole, used by whalers from the 17th-18th centuries and later developed for coal mining; recognized as Norwegian territory in 1920.

xue-long.name: Xue Long
xue-long.summary: A Chinese icebreaking research vessel built in 1993, which was China's only polar research icebreaker until a second ship joined it in 2019.

xue-long-2.name: Xue Long 2
xue-long-2.summary: A Chinese icebreaking research vessel that entered service in 2019 as the more capable successor to the original Xue Long.

petermann-glacier.name: Petermann Glacier
petermann-glacier.summary: Large glacier in northwest Greenland linking the ice sheet to the Arctic Ocean, named after cartographer August Heinrich Petermann; it has shed several major icebergs in recent decades.

nuuk.name: Nuuk
nuuk.summary: Capital and largest city of Greenland, founded in 1728 by Danish-Norwegian missionary Hans Egede as Godthaab; renamed Nuuk after home rule began in 1979.

university-of-greenland.name: University of Greenland
university-of-greenland.summary: Greenland's only university, based in the capital Nuuk, teaching mainly in Danish with a small enrollment since most Greenlandic students study in Denmark instead.

aarhus.name: Aarhus
aarhus.summary: Denmark's second-largest city, founded as a Viking-age harbour settlement in the late 8th century and today home to the country's longest cathedral.

international-polar-year.name: International Polar Year
international-polar-year.summary: A series of internationally coordinated polar research efforts, first held in 1882–1883, with later editions in 1932–1933, 1957–58, and 2007–2009.

china-iceland-arctic-science-observatory.name: China-Iceland Arctic Science Observatory
china-iceland-arctic-science-observatory.summary: A joint Chinese-Icelandic research facility in Kárhóll, northern Iceland, opened in 2018 to study the Arctic, run by China's Polar Research Institute and Iceland's research center.

riometer.name: Riometer
riometer.summary: An instrument that measures how much the ionosphere absorbs cosmic radio noise, used to detect increased ionization in the upper atmosphere.

polar-research-institute-of-china.name: Polar Research Institute of China
polar-research-institute-of-china.summary: China's main state institute for polar science, based in Shanghai, which runs research stations in Antarctica and the Arctic and two icebreaking research vessels.

icelandic-centre-for-research.name: Icelandic Centre for Research
icelandic-centre-for-research.summary: An Icelandic government body, formed in 2003, that funds scientific research and coordinates Iceland's participation in European research, education and culture programmes.

vinland-map.name: Vinland Map
vinland-map.summary: A 20th-century forgery presented as a 15th-century map showing Norse exploration of North America; publicized as genuine in 1965 but declared a modern forgery by Yale specialists in 2018.

terra-nullius.name: Terra nullius
terra-nullius.summary: A Latin legal principle meaning 'nobody's land,' used since the 19th century to justify claiming territory not held by a recognized sovereign state, including land where indigenous peoples lived.

erik-the-red-s-land.name: Erik the Red's Land
erik-the-red-s-land.summary: An area of eastern Greenland claimed by Norway in the early 1930s and named for Erik the Red; an international court ruled against Norway's claim in 1933.

permanent-court-of-international-justice.name: Permanent Court of International Justice
permanent-court-of-international-justice.summary: An international court attached to the League of Nations from 1922 to 1946, issuing judgments and advisory opinions before being replaced by the International Court of Justice.

folketing.name: Folketing
folketing.summary: Denmark's national parliament, established in 1849, whose 179 members pass laws, approve the state budget and government, and can force ministers or the whole cabinet to resign.

henrik-kauffmann.name: Henrik Kauffmann
henrik-kauffmann.summary: Danish ambassador to the United States during World War II (1888 to 1963), who signed over part of Greenland to the US.

three-year-expedition-to-east-greenland.name: Three-year Expedition to East Greenland
three-year-expedition-to-east-greenland.summary: A 1931 to 1934 Danish scientific expedition, funded by the Carlsberg Foundation and the Danish state, that mapped and named many geographic features of East Greenland.

lauge-koch.name: Lauge Koch
lauge-koch.summary: Danish geologist and Arctic explorer, 1892 to 1964.

carlsberg-foundation.name: Carlsberg Foundation
carlsberg-foundation.summary: A Danish nonprofit founded in 1876 by J. C. Jacobsen to fund the Carlsberg Laboratory and, later, scientific research more broadly, using profits from the Carlsberg Brewery.

monroe-doctrine.name: Monroe Doctrine
monroe-doctrine.summary: A US foreign policy declared by President James Monroe in 1823 opposing European interference in the Americas, later used to justify American dominance across the hemisphere.

pituffik-space-base.name: Pituffik Space Base
pituffik-space-base.summary: A US Space Force base on Greenland's northwest coast, formerly called Thule Air Base until renamed in 2023; the northernmost US Department of Defense installation.

angakkuq.name: Angakkuq
angakkuq.summary: A spiritual and intellectual figure in Inuit culture who serves a role similar to a medicine man or shaman, with comparable figures found among other Alaska Native peoples.

inughuit.name: Inughuit
inughuit.summary: An ethnic subgroup of Greenlandic Inuit, the northernmost group of Inuit and people in North America, making up about 1% of Greenland's population.

missionary-oblates-of-mary-immaculate.name: Missionary Oblates of Mary Immaculate
missionary-oblates-of-mary-immaculate.summary: A Catholic missionary congregation founded in 1816 by Eugène de Mazenod, known for missionary work including among Indigenous peoples in Canada.

little-sisters-of-jesus.name: Little Sisters of Jesus
little-sisters-of-jesus.summary: A community of Catholic religious sisters inspired by the life and writings of Charles de Foucauld, founded by Little Sister Magdeleine of Jesus (Madeleine Hutin).

aasiaat.name: Aasiaat
aasiaat.summary: A town on Disko Bay in western Greenland, also known as Egedesminde, and Greenland's fifth-largest town.

narsaq.name: Narsaq
narsaq.summary: A town in Kujalleq, southern Greenland, on the shores of Tunulliarfik Fjord, formerly known as Nordprøven.

church-of-greenland.name: Church of Greenland
church-of-greenland.summary: The official Lutheran church of Greenland, a semi-independent diocese of the Church of Denmark led by its own bishop since 2020.

church-of-denmark.name: Church of Denmark
church-of-denmark.summary: Denmark's established Evangelical Lutheran national church, headed by the monarch and Parliament, with about 70% of Danes as members as of 2026.

kangeq.name: Kangeq
kangeq.summary: A former settlement in southwestern Greenland, on the island where the first Danish-Norwegian colony was founded between 1721 and 1728.

church-of-the-faroe-islands.name: Church of the Faroe Islands
church-of-the-faroe-islands.summary: The Faroe Islands' established Evangelical Lutheran church, one of the world's smallest state churches, independent since 2007 after being a diocese of the Church of Denmark.

vivian-motzfeldt.name: Vivian Motzfeldt
vivian-motzfeldt.summary: Greenlandic politician (born 1972) who served as Greenland's Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2022 to 2026 and previously as speaker of its parliament and chairwoman of the Siumut party.

qaqortoq.name: Qaqortoq
qaqortoq.summary: The capital city of the Kujalleq municipality in southern Greenland, located near the site of the Norse Eastern Settlement founded by Icelandic colonists.

upernaviarsuk.name: Upernaviarsuk
upernaviarsuk.summary: An agricultural settlement in Kujalleq, Greenland.

pope-benedict-xvi.name: Pope Benedict XVI
pope-benedict-xvi.summary: Born Joseph Ratzinger, a theologian who became head of the Catholic Church from 2005 until resigning in 2013, having long been a close adviser to John Paul II.
